questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 + 18}{x(x^2 + 9)}$, express $f(x)$ in partial fractions. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The denominator has the linear factor $x$ and the irreducible quadratic factor $x^2 + 9$, so the form is

$$\frac{x^2 + 18}{x(x^2 + 9)} \equiv \frac{A}{x} + \frac{Bx + C}{x^2 + 9}.$$

Multiply through by $x(x^2 + 9)$:

$$x^2 + 18 \equiv A(x^2 + 9) + (Bx + C)x.$$

- $x = 0$: $18 = 9A$, so $A = 2$.
- Coefficient of $x^2$: $1 = A + B = 2 + B$, so $B = -1$.
- Coefficient of $x$: $0 = C$, so $C = 0$.
- Constant term: $18 = 9A$, consistent.

$$\boxed{f(x) = \frac{2}{x} - \frac{x}{x^2 + 9}}$$

Check at $x = 3$: $f(3) = \dfrac{27}{3 \times 18} = \dfrac12$ and $\dfrac23 - \dfrac{3}{18} = \dfrac23 - \dfrac16 = \dfrac12$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 + 18}{x(x^2 + 9)}$, hence or otherwise, show that $\displaystyle\int_2^4 f(x)\,dx = \ln\left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{13}}{5}\right)$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use $f(x) = \dfrac2x - \dfrac{x}{x^2 + 9}$ from part (a). For the second term, $\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln(x^2 + 9) = \dfrac{2x}{x^2 + 9}$, so $\displaystyle\int\frac{x}{x^2 + 9}\,dx = \tfrac12\ln(x^2 + 9)$. Hence

$$\int_2^4 f(x)\,dx = \left[\,2\ln x - \tfrac12\ln(x^2 + 9)\,\right]_2^4.$$

Upper limit $x = 4$: $2\ln 4 - \tfrac12\ln 25 = 2\ln 4 - \ln 5$.

Lower limit $x = 2$: $2\ln 2 - \tfrac12\ln 13$.

Subtract:

$$\int_2^4 f(x)\,dx = 2\ln 4 - \ln 5 - 2\ln 2 + \tfrac12\ln 13 = 2\ln\frac42 - \ln 5 + \tfrac12\ln 13 = \ln 4 - \ln 5 + \ln\sqrt{13}.$$

Combining the logarithms:

$$\int_2^4 f(x)\,dx = \ln\left(\frac{4\sqrt{13}}{5}\right). \qquad \blacksquare$$

Numerical check: $\dfrac{4\sqrt{13}}{5} = 2.8844$ and $\ln 2.8844 = 1.0593$, which equals the value of the integral computed numerically.
